items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: Gladys Hampton called to me... She said, 'We don't pay anybody that kind of money...'

ctx.x: You were with Hampton. And there's a kind of a -- sort of a public image with Hampton as a happy go lucky, not especially bright guy that could swing good. Is

No. He's a very dishonest man, and his wife -- he and his wife made millions of dollars off of hiring unknown musicians out in the sticks for little or no money, promise them one salary, get them out on the road and says, Lionel Hampton has the right to promise that kind of money. I was promised -- Lionel guaranteed me $400 a week when I first joined the band. And so I got on the road, I was very far away from California, and Gladys Hampton called to me and he says, why, we could pay that kind of money. No one --…
Gee, and you had to pay your other stuff besides.
